hits.title: Our Vision
hits.snippet:
Plant Sciences Genetics® (PSG) is a premier agricultural research company that breeds and propagates berry crops for the global marketplace.
PSG and its affiliates hold more than 50 plant patents and plant breeder’s rights certificates for strawberry and raspberry, and supply plants of its proprietary varieties to leading growers in over 50 countries.
PSG is also aggressively preparing for its first commercial releases of blackberry and blueberry varieties.
...
Plant Sciences Genetics® (PSG) traces its roots back to the humble beginnings of Plant Sciences Inc.
(PSI), founded by Richard Nelson in Watsonville, California in 1985.
Richard's passion for science and agriculture led him to UC Davis, where he met his future wife, Vicki, and eventually earned his doctorate in entomology.
Richard spent 18 years in the berry industry and realized he had a strong entrepreneurial spirit.
This realization led to the formation of Plant Sciences Inc., which initially focused on contract research.
Over the first 15 years, PSI completed 150-250 agronomic and crop protection research projects, helping the company establish its reputation.
Eventually, this research evolved into a series of breeding programs and nursery operations across strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and even artichokes for a while.
As Plant Sciences and its affiliated breeding programs grew, Richard's sons Steve and Mike became integral parts of the business.
Steve now leads the business as CEO and Mike manages the science side as Chief Science Officer.
Together, they lead Plant Sciences’ proprietary breeding programs, nursery operations, technology partners, and licensing partnerships.
As of 2023, Plant Sciences, had established 15 distinct berry breeding programs with nurseries in the US and Mexico, plus, a master license partner in Europe.
In 2024, Plant Sciences consolidated its breeding program and opened up previously exclusive breeding programs to the open market, under the new name, Plant Sciences Genetics.
Looking ahead, PSG aims to be a global provider of genetics, introducing competitive varieties worldwide.
With partnerships like Simplot investing in PSG, the company is poised to continue its growth, connected to growers, retailers, and consumers alike.
The company's success lies in its ability to couple agronomic performance with consumer acceptance, to successfully serve growers while also engaging buyers and consumers.
Richard Nelson's vision and entrepreneurial spirit have transformed Plant Sciences from a small contract research firm into a global leader in berry genetics.
...
Committed to developing best-in-class berry genetics that enable ALL BERRIES FOR ALL MARKETS, Plant Sciences Genetics® (PSG) has emerged as a premier agricultural research company with emphasis on plant breeding and propagation of berry crops for the global marketplace.

**
WATSONVILLE, Calif., August 1, 2023 (Newswire.com)
-
** Plant Sciences, Inc.
(PSI) and its affiliate berry breeding interests today announced that they are restructuring to form a new entity, Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc.
(PSG), that will serve North American and key international berry markets with its portfolio of strawberry, raspberry, blackberry, blueberry, and black raspberry genetics.
PSG will hold all berry breeding populations and related intellectual property previously held by Plant Sciences, Berry Genetics, Strawberry Sciences, Via Berry Breeding, Vitae Caneberry Breeding, and Fragaria Plant Sciences.
In total, PSG will consist of 15 distinct breeding populations consisting of eight strawberry, three blueberry, two raspberry, one blackberry, and one black raspberry.
The newly formed entity will be able to deliver its berry varieties to an expanded number of growers and marketers throughout North America and key international markets.
PSI will serve PSG, under contract, providing research and propagation services to the new entity.
"We are highly motivated to serve and engage with new customers, offering licensed access to our ever-expanding portfolio of competitive berry varieties to the broader open market for the first time.
While embracing this opportunity, we remain committed to the success of those we have served for many years," said Steve Nelson, Chief Executive Officer of Plant Sciences, Inc.

# GM Strawberry
## Market Status
**The company Simplot is selling a very limited quantity of genetically engineered (genetically modified or GM) gene-edited strawberries in the US only, but is seeking to increase the GM strawberry’s commercial reach in both the US and Canada.** The gene-edited strawberries are only being sold through Simplot’s Wholesale Foodservice division in the US.
...
## The GM Strawberry
The US agriculture company Simplot and the biotechnology company Plant Sciences, Inc.
have partnered to genetically modify strawberries using the new genetic engineering techniques of gene editing:
1. In 2021, Simplot announced it would use gene editing to try to develop strawberries with extended shelf-life.
2. In December 2024, Simplot stated its intention to start selling a gene-edited strawberry in Canada as soon as 2025, gene-edited for a longer harvest season (remontant), however its commercial release in Canada is stalled.
( “Everbearing” (remontant) strawberry varieties that flower and set fruit multiple times during a season have already been created through traditional breeding and are common in gardens and farms across Canada.)
3. In early 2026, Simplot confirmed that a very limited quantity of its gene-edited strawberries were being sold through its Wholesale Foodservice division in the US only.
Plant Sciences Inc.
says “PSI is also aggressively preparing for its first commercial releases of blackberry and blueberry varieties.”
Simplot has not yet responded to inquiries from CBAN.
**Gene editing**, or genome editing, is a collection of new genetic engineering (genetic modification or GM) techniques that alter the genetic material (usually DNA) of plants, animals and other organisms.

hits.title: Companies planning gene-edited strawberries to reduce waste
hits.snippet:
Two companies announced on Thursday they are planning on gene-editing strawberries to reduce waste.
J.R.
Simplot Company and Plant Sciences Inc.
(PSI) announced they are expecting to produce the first commercially available, gene-edited strawberries in the next few years.
The goal for the gene-edited strawberries is to reduce waste by making the strawberries have a longer shelf life.

# Plant Sciences Inc. / Plant Sciences Genetics investigation

**Cut-off: 20 October 2026 inclusive.**

## Executive findings

| Question | Finding as of 20 October 2026 | Confidence / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Official domain | The current public-facing PSG domain is **[plantsciencesgenetics.com](https://www.plantsciencesgenetics.com/)**. The legacy domain **[plantsciences.com](https://plantsciences.com/)** now also presents Plant Sciences Genetics and promotes Rejoice. | High: both domains display PSG content. [1][2] |
| PSI legal identity | **Plant Sciences, Inc.**, a **California corporation**, founded in Watsonville in 1985; address **342 Green Valley Road, Watsonville, CA 95076**. | High: company history plus USPTO record identifying “Plant Sciences, Inc. (CORPORATION; CALIFORNIA).” [1][11] |
| PSG legal identity | **Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc.**, a **Delaware corporation**, at the same Watsonville address. It was announced on **1 August 2023** as a newly formed entity consolidating berry breeding populations and IP. | High: company announcement and USPTO record identifying “Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc. (CORPORATION; Delaware).” [4][11] |
| PSI versus PSG | They should **not** be treated merely as two names for one legal entity. PSG holds the consolidated breeding populations and related berry IP; PSI was announced as providing PSG research and propagation under contract. Public marketing increasingly uses PSG as the operating brand. | High. [4] |
| Parent / ownership | No ultimate parent has been publicly established. The PSG site says “Simplot investing in PSG,” but discloses no percentage, date, consideration, governance rights or financing round. | Investment relationship likely; ownership extent **not established in this research pass**. [153] |
| Subsidiaries | **Plant Sciences Europe B.V.**, established in the Netherlands in 2016, was expressly described as PSI’s “wholly-owned subsidiary.” A Spanish **Plant Sciences Europe S.L.** record identifies Plant Sciences Europe B.V. as sole shareholder. | High for these two entities historically; whether ownership moved to PSG after consolidation is **not established**. [266][270] |
| Gene editing | PSG/PSI has genuine gene-editing programs with **Simplot in strawberry** and **Pairwise in caneberries**. That does **not** mean every PSG variety is edited: PSG also conducts conventional crossing, marker-assisted selection, tissue culture, field evaluation and post-harvest selection. | High. [43][61][73][307] |
| Commercial edited products | A very limited quantity of Simplot’s edited remontant strawberries was reportedly sold through Simplot’s U.S. wholesale-foodservice division by early 2026. Pairwise reported edited blackberry sales in Colombia, while Fontana was announced on 14 October 2026; the precise identity of the Colombian product and its equivalence to Fontana are not completely documented. | Mixed: U.S. strawberry sale comes from CBAN reporting Simplot confirmation; Pairwise itself reports Colombian sales. [49][64][74] |
| Conventional PSG products | VS-60 strawberry and Rejoice blackberry are commercially introduced PSG cultivars. Nothing found establishes either as gene-edited; they should be treated as conventionally bred unless PSG discloses otherwise. | High that commercial; editing status **not established**. [181][203][336] |
| Fall Creek, Planasa, Plantik and HRB | No corporate, licensing or breeding relationship with PSI/PSG was established for these companies. They are separate breeders/technology developers. Plantik–Hudson River have their own heat-tolerant strawberry project; Fall Creek has its own blueberry/Rubus genetics; Planasa is an EW Group subsidiary with its own breeding programs. | High as to absence of found evidence; a private undisclosed agreement cannot be excluded. [76][91][106][315] |

---

## 1. Identity, aliases and corporate structure

| Entity / alias | Legal or operational status | Relationship and dated evidence | Short exact supporting excerpt / attribution | Evidence gap or conflict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Plant Sciences, Inc. (PSI)** | California corporation; legacy operating/research company | Founded by Richard Nelson in Watsonville in **1985**. | PSG history: “**PSI, founded by Richard Nelson in Watsonville, California in 1985**.” [1] | California entity number and current shareholder register were not established. |
| **Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc. (PSG)** | Delaware corporation; current consolidated genetics entity and brand | Formation announced **1 Aug. 2023**; company history calls the open-market consolidation a 2024 change. | PSI announcement: “**restructuring to form a new entity, Plant Sciences Genetics, Inc. (PSG)**.” [4] | The apparent 2023 formation versus “in 2024” operating transition is a timing distinction, not necessarily a contradiction. |
| **Plant Sciences Genetics® / PSG℠** | Trademark/brand usage | Used for breeding, propagation, research and commercialization. | Official site calls PSG “**a premier agricultural research company that breeds and propagates berry crops**.” [169] | Exact trademark-registration status of every PSG-form mark not exhaustively verified. |
| **Plant Sciences** | Informal/legacy group name | Used in historical materials for PSI and affiliated breeding interests. | 2023 announcement distinguishes “Plant Sciences” from the other breeding interests whose assets moved to PSG. [33] | Do not infer that every occurrence denotes the same corporation. |
| **Berry Genetics, Inc.** | Historical affiliated breeding/IP holder | Its breeding populations and IP were announced as moving into PSG. | PSG would hold IP “previously held by **Plant Sciences, Berry Genetics, Strawberry Sciences, Via Berry Breeding, Vitae Caneberry Breeding, and Fragaria Plant Sciences**.” [22] | Ownership percentage and continuing legal existence not established. |
| **Strawberry Sciences, LLC** | Historical affiliate/program holder | Included in PSG consolidation. In 2020 it was named among PSI affiliate companies in Europe. | Plant Sciences Europe plans covered programs of “**Berry Genetics, Inc, Strawberry Sciences, LLC and Fragaria Plant Sciences BV**.” [266] | Current status not established. |
| **Via Berry Breeding** | Historical breeding interest; source of PSG’s VIA program | Included in consolidation. VS-60 later became the first patented commercial release from the **VIA breeding program**. | VS-60: “**first patented commercial strawberry release from PSG’s VIA breeding program**.” [181] | Exact legal suffix and former ownership were not established. |
| **Vitae Caneberry Breeding** | Historical breeding interest | Included in consolidation. | Listed in the 2023 restructuring announcement. [265] | Legal form and present status not established. |
| **Fragaria Plant Sciences / Fragaria Plant Sciences B.V.** | Historical breeding interest/entity | Included in consolidation; previously named in European program expansion. | Listed in the 2023 restructuring and 2020 European subsidiary report. [265][266] | Current registration/ownership not established. |
| **Plant Sciences Europe B.V. (PSE)** | Dutch private limited company; historically wholly owned by PSI | Established in **2016** to serve Europe/UK. | “PSI established its **wholly-owned subsidiary, Plant Sciences Europe BV (PSE), in the Netherlands in 2016**.” [266] | Whether PSE is now directly owned by PSI, PSG or another holding entity is **not established**. |
| **Plant Sciences Europe S.L.** | Spanish subsidiary | Spanish record identifies PSE B.V. as sole shareholder; business includes selecting, reproducing and licensing plant varieties. | “**Socio único: PLANT SCIENCES EUROPE B V**.” [270] | Current operating scope and capitalization not established. |
| **Plant Sciences Inc. of Gormley, Ontario** | Unrelated turf/fertilizer company acquired by BrettYoung | Must be excluded from the Watsonville corporate family. | BrettYoung acquired “**Plant Science Inc. of Gormley, Ontario**” in 2016. [157] | None; name collision only. |

### Restructuring scope

The 2023 announcement said PSG would receive **15 breeding populations**: eight strawberry, three blueberry, two raspberry, one blackberry and one black-raspberry population. PSI would remain a contractual research and propagation provider. [4] A 2024 interview instead described **17 programs**—ten strawberry, three blueberry, two raspberry, one blackberry and one black raspberry. [281] The likely explanation is two additional strawberry programs or a different counting method, but PSG did not reconcile the figures; the exact current count is therefore **not established**.

The same announcement claimed more than **80 proprietary varieties**—58 strawberry, 17 raspberry and three blackberry—whereas PSG’s current history says it and its affiliates hold **more than 50 patents and breeder-right certificates**, specifically for strawberry and raspberry. These are not equivalent metrics: “varieties” versus issued rights/certificates, and potentially a different affiliate perimeter. [33][31]

---

## 2. Headquarters versus program and nursery geography

| Geography | Function / evidence | Status by cut-off |
|---|---|---|
| **342 Green Valley Road, Watsonville, California** | Shared PSI/PSG headquarters and research address; CDFA lists Plant Sciences Genetics, Incorporated as a licensed nursery there. [11][41] | Established HQ/legal address. |
| **Macdoel, California** | Historical high-elevation nursery/propagation location at 234 Juniper Knoll Road. [25] | Historical/current operation suggested, but present PSG ownership and exact role not independently confirmed. |
| **Manteca, California** | Historical nursery propagation location. [25] | Current operating status not established. |
| **Central Mexico** | PSG job description says PSG operates its own nurseries in California and central Mexico. [10] | Established at general-region level; exact corporate entity and site not found. |
| **Watsonville, Santa Maria, Oxnard and Baja California** | 2023 grower meetings; VS-60 demonstrated performance in Oxnard, Santa Maria and Baja. [4][181] | Commercial-development regions, not additional headquarters. |
| **Netherlands** | Plant Sciences Europe B.V., established 2016 to serve Europe and the UK. [266] | Regional corporate/commercial base. |
| **Spain—Lucena del Puerto, Huelva; Segovia** | El Pinar evaluates Plant Sciences/Berry Genetics strawberry material at Huelva and summer strawberry/raspberry/blueberry programs in Segovia. [189] | Partner trial/development sites, not PSG HQ. |
| **Portugal** | El Pinar experimentation center for raspberries and blueberries. [189] | Partner program site. |
| **Spain, Portugal, Romania** | El Pinar plant-production fields and distribution footprint; it has been a PSI/Berry Genetics licensee for more than 20 years. [286] | Licensed propagation/commercial geography. |
| **Southern Europe and North Africa** | El Pinar is described as exclusive licensee for PSI/Berry Genetics programs; Victory was available to growers across this region. [291] | Commercial-license territory. |
| **Global / 50+ countries** | PSG says proprietary plants are supplied to leading growers in more than 50 countries and field evaluations occur in growers’ fields worldwide. [31][73] | Broad claim; country-by-country variety availability is not public. |
| **Colombia** | Pairwise reported the first commercial sale of edited blackberries in Colombia in 2025/early 2026. [64] | Commercial edited-blackberry geography; precise cultivar and PSG royalty structure not disclosed. |
| **England** | Simplot planned 2026 selection trials of eight TFL1-edited strawberry lines before commercial production and registration. [51] | Trial/selection geography, not yet established as commercial by the cut-off. |

---

## 3. What is conventional breeding, advanced breeding and gene editing?

| Method | PSI/PSG evidence | What may safely be concluded |
|---|---|---|
| **Conventional crossing and phenotypic selection** | PSG says it uses “**traditional crossing techniques, and other technologies**,” followed by field and simulated shipping/handling evaluations. [73] | Core strawberry, raspberry, blackberry and blueberry programs are not automatically gene-edited. |
| **Marker-assisted selection / molecular breeding** | A PSI patent application describes SNP markers for Fusarium, Macrophomina and Colletotrichum resistance, remontancy and berry weight. [307] A former PSI scientist described marker-assisted seedling selection for strawberry, blueberry, blackberry, raspberry and artichoke. [38] | Advanced selection is demonstrated, but marker use does not itself edit DNA. |
| **Tissue culture / clean propagation** | PSG says plants are propagated through tissue culture for disease-free, uniform starts. [2] | Propagation technology, not breeding or editing. |
| **Field and post-harvest testing** | PSG says varieties are evaluated in grower fields worldwide and quality tests simulate shipping and handling. [73] | Demonstrated evaluation process; “field-tested” must not be conflated with “commercial.” |
| **Simplot CRISPR strawberry** | Simplot uses CRISPR/Cas9, delivered either by Agrobacterium or ribonucleoprotein methods, to knock out multiple alleles; selected lines contain no introduced CRISPR DNA. [47] | Real gene editing, initially demonstrated for TFL1/remontancy. |
| **Pairwise CRISPR caneberries** | Pairwise uses Fulcrum CRISPR tools and PSI/PSG germplasm. Published work describes a platform to transform and edit tetraploid blackberry and characterize first edited events. [61][70] | Gene editing is demonstrated in blackberry; individual PSG commercial cultivars cannot be labeled edited without product-specific evidence. |
| **Ohalo Boosted Breeding™** | Ohalo describes offspring receiving the entire genome from both parents rather than a random half. [137] Secondary reporting says gene editing is used to alter parental reproductive circuits. [140] | **Do not equate “Boosted Breeding” with ordinary CRISPR trait editing.** It is an Ohalo reproductive/breeding system that may use editing during creation of parent lines. No PSI/PSG–Ohalo agreement or PSG Boosted berry was established. |
| **Plantik ATLANTIS + HRB BioMaas** | Plantik searches non-coding regulatory DNA with ATLANTIS; HRB supplies transgene-free strawberry editing through BioMaas for a heat-tolerance project. [76][81] | Separate Plantik–HRB project. No PSI/PSG germplasm, license or participation established. |

---

## 4. Principal partnerships, licenses and non-relationships

| Organization | Dated relationship with PSI/PSG | Crops / traits / technology | Announced, demonstrated or commercial? | IP/license evidence and gaps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **J.R. Simplot Company** | Collaboration dates to **2011**; strategic gene-editing alliance announced **28 Oct. 2021**. PSG now says Simplot is “investing in PSG.” [43][153] | Strawberry; initially framed around shelf life, reduced waste and yield, with demonstrated **TFL1 knockout/remontancy**. Simplot methods include CRISPR/Cas9 Agrobacterium and RNP delivery. [46][47] | Announced 2021; regulator-reviewed 2020 onward; limited U.S. foodservice sale reported by early 2026; UK lines in 2026 selection trials. | Simplot licensed foundational CRISPR-Cas9 tools from Corteva and Broad Institute in 2018. [53] PSG ownership, royalty and cultivar-license terms are undisclosed. |
| **Pairwise** | Public/private Rubus research partnership by **2019**; product partnership announced **15 Apr. 2020**. [217][62] | Black raspberry, red raspberry and blackberry; taste, convenience, shelf life and off-season availability. PSI supplied germplasm and nursery propagation; Pairwise supplied editing. | Transformation/editing demonstrated; seedless/thornless/compact blackberry demonstrated by 2024; edited-blackberry commercial sale in Colombia reported in 2026; Fontana announced 14 Oct. 2026. [213][64][74] | Pairwise uses its Fulcrum CRISPR platform. Exact PSG cultivar, edit targets and economics for Fontana are undisclosed. |
| **USDA-ARS, University of Arkansas, Cornell, NC State** | Collaborative Rubus-diversity project announced in 2019/2020. | More than 300 Rubus species/accessions; genomes, resequencing, phenotyping; natural variation for breeding/editing. [217] | Research and two-year field-testing program, not a commercial product. | Public-line data were intended to be shared. Product IP allocation not found. |
| **El Pinar** | More than 20-year license and development relationship with PSI and Berry Genetics. [286] | Strawberry, raspberry, blackberry and blueberry; European/Mediterranean testing and propagation. | Numerous conventional varieties commercial, including Victory, Primavera, Inspire and Renewal. | Described as exclusive licensee for Southern Europe/North Africa; complete contract and territorial exceptions unavailable. [291] |
| **The Greenery** | Exclusive agreement reported **10 May 2019**. | Joint development of strawberry, raspberry and blackberry varieties emphasizing taste, shelf life and yield. [88] | Development and exclusive grower marketing opportunity announced; variety-by-variety rights not disclosed. | Current continuation after PSG open-market restructuring not established. |
| **Gem-Pack Berries** | Field-tested Rejoice before launch; by Oct. 2026 marketed Rejoice fruit and IFPA samples with PSG. [327] | Rejoice blackberry. | Field-tested and commercially packed in clamshells. | Contract/territory not disclosed. |
| **Fall Creek Farm & Nursery** | **No PSI/PSG relationship established.** | Separate blueberry breeder; by 2026 expanding into Rubus through Berryplant/Berrytech acquisition. [91] | Its Sekoya and Fall Creek Collection varieties are separate commercial programs. | Do not assign Fall Creek varieties or trials to PSG. |
| **Planasa / EW Group** | **No PSI/PSG partnership or ownership established.** A 2026 photo caption placing “Planasa Plant Sciences Europe BV” together is too ambiguous to prove a transaction. [310] | Planasa independently breeds strawberries, raspberries, blackberries and blueberries through conventional and molecular-marker-assisted methods. [106][111] | Independent commercial breeder. EW Group acquired Planasa in 2023. [321] | No license, shareholding or PSG product connection found. |
| **Plantik Biosciences** | No PSG tie established. | ATLANTIS machine-learning target discovery in regulatory/non-coding DNA. [80] | Heat-tolerance targets validated in tomato; strawberry validation work announced with HRB. | Any PSG germplasm or commercial breeder license is **not established**. |
| **Hudson River Biotechnology (HRB)** | No PSG tie established. It separately licensed Pairwise’s Fulcrum platform in May 202
